To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

behavioural profiles of non demented patients with amyotrophic lateral scleroses (ALS) are heterogenous, that we identified three behavioural profiles (disinhibition/hostility, apathy and dysexecutivity) in ALS patients, that we found a correlation between the cortical atrophy and the behavioural profiles, and that we confirmed the reliability of a behavioural profile that overlaps the behavioural variant of frontotemporo dementia (FTD).

(1) we identified three behavioural profiles in non-demented ALS patients, (2) each profile was associated with different patterns of cortical atrophy and (3) these findings were comparable with those reported in the behavioural-variant frontotemporal lobe dementia

different behavioural profiles could reliably be identified in non-demented ALS patients and that the right frontotemporocingular thinning was the most important correlate of the behavioural profile overlapping that described in behavioural-variant frontotemporal lobe dementia (bvFTDL).
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the behavioural profile of patients with ALS.
the identification of the cortical correlates of the different behavioural phenotypes in non-demented ALS patients and the comparison with the findings of the literature in bvFTD patients.
the study of the neurobiological correlates of behaviour changes in ALS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

behavioural changes in patients with ALS are not a simple reflection of the underlying motor impairment but rather a complex and multifaceted phenomenon that is likely to reflect a specific neurobiological substrate, which is different from that of bvFTD.
the right frontotempral and cingular cortex is a hallmark of bvFTD, and this is true also in ALS patients.
our results suggest that the cortical thinning of the right frontotemproal cortex is a hallmark of behavioural changes in patients with ALS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the behavioural changes of non-dementing patients with ALS are heterogeneous and that the right frontotemporopolar cortex atrophy could be a marker for a behavioural profile overlapping that reported in bvFTD.
behavioural changes in ALS are heterogeneous and can be grouped into different clusters.
behavioural profiles in ALS are not homogeneous and are related to different cortical areas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the behavioural profiles of patients with ALS are heterogeneous, with some resembling those reported in patients with bvFTD.
behavioural changes in patients with ALS are not a random collection of behavioural symptoms but rather a specific behavioural phenotype, which is related to the cortical atrophy.
the right frontotemporopolar cortex plays a crucial role in the development of behavioural disturbances of patients with ALS.
